game: DEN@NYJ Week 6 2025, kickoff 2025-10-12 09:30 ET, outdoors, NYJ +7.5, total 43.5

script.base: Denver is a 7.5-point favorite with implied totals DEN 25.5 and NYJ 18.0 on a 43.5 total, so the book expects Denver to lead by about a touchdown in a moderate-pace game, not a shootout. Base flow: Denver leans on J.K. Dobbins (47 carries, 263 yards, 5.6 YPC over weeks 3-5) to stay ahead and run late, while the Jets, as a 7.5-point dog, throw to Garrett Wilson (31 targets, 237 yards, 288 air yards) and Mason Taylor (25 targets, 150 yards) to stay in it. Justin Fields' legs (13 carries, 108 yards in that window) are the Jets' counterpunch, not a second featured rushing line.
script.flip1: It stays competitive into the fourth. Fields' rushing and a Denver line without G Ben Powers keep NYJ within a score, so Dobbins never gets a pure clock-kill quarter and both passing games stay live for four quarters.
script.flip2: Denver jumps ahead by 17-plus early. NYJ abandons Breece Hall (37 carries, 215 yards over weeks 3-5), his rush line dies, and if the margin gets ugly Denver's skill starters lose late snaps. That is a live flip but not the base case at only -7.5.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report, inactives not locked (Roach and Stephens still Questionable; re-run if either is inactive about 90 minutes before kick). DEN G Ben Powers Out (Biceps): pressure and quick throws up, rushing efficiency and deep WR yards down, RB/TE catches up — a direct ding on Dobbins' YPC and on Courtland Sutton/Troy Franklin/Marvin Mims air yards, a small boost for Evan Engram and RJ Harvey catches. DEN LB Jonah Elliss Out (Ribs): missing linebacker helps NYJ TE/RB, so Mason Taylor and Breece Hall's receiving routes face a backup. DEN DT Malcolm Roach Questionable (Calf): if he sits, Denver's 4.23 YPC run defense softens for Hall. NYJ WR Allen Lazard Out (personal): only 6 targets and 24 yards over weeks 3-5, so a small redistribution to Wilson, Taylor, Josh Reynolds and Isaiah Davis, not a new WR1. NYJ CB Michael Carter II Out (Concussion): slot corner missing, which helps Denver's TE/slot/RB receiving (Engram, Mims, Harvey) more than outside Sutton. NYJ CB Brandon Stephens Questionable (Neck): if he sits, Sutton's outside matchup gets easier; he is not confirmed out. NYJ LB Ja'Markis Weston Out (Groin): another missing linebacker in front of Denver's TE/RB. Sources: pack injury report plus weeks 3-5 target/carry counts.

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone rates are not in the pack, so no shell is assigned. What is known: NYJ blitzes 34% and Denver's EPA/dropback is better vs the blitz (0.19) than vs no blitz (0.09), so Nix is not a check-down-only QB when pressured. Denver blitzes 30% and NYJ EPA/dropback falls from 0.09 with no blitz to 0.03 when blitzed.
matchup.pressure: NYJ 34% blitz does not profile as a Denver deep-game killer on the EPA split above. The real pressure flag is structural: Powers out should still speed up Denver's dropback and cut Sutton/Franklin/Mims deep yards even if the blitz number itself is friendly. Denver's 30% blitz is a mild negative for Fields, which can push check-downs toward Taylor and Hall rather than holding the ball.
matchup.bleeds: NYJ defense, 5 games: 4.79 rush YPC, 14 runs of 10+, 19 passes of 20+ for 147 yards. YPA left 7.33 (55 att), middle 4.77 (22), right 8.94 (63). They bleed outside and on the ground; the middle is the tight area. Denver defense, 5 games: 4.23 rush YPC, only 6 runs of 10+, 13 passes of 20+ for 193 yards. YPA left 5.29 (66), middle 6.56 (36), right 7.83 (70). Denver is the sturdier run defense and bleeds right and, relatively, the middle.
matchup.overlap: Two real overlaps, one conflict. Dobbins is the run engine against the defense that allows 4.79 YPC and 14 chunk runs — that is the clean primary-weapon overlap, and the -7.5 script feeds it. Sutton is the pass primary (24 targets, 298 yards, 302 air yards in weeks 3-5; the weeks 3-5 games add to 118+81+99) against the outside bleed and 19 explosives, but Powers out plus a Denver lead-and-run script both cut deep WR yards, so that overlap is not stamped. The number that is actually off the usage is Mason Taylor (25 targets, 150 yards, 137 air yards, 6.0 yards per target) into a Denver defense missing LB Elliss, with Denver's middle at 6.56 YPA.

Two of those three cleared 79.5 and 79 missed by half a yard; average 87.7. Harvey is the change-of-pace (20/72 rush, 11 targets, 72 rec yards), last4 rush 8, 2, 58, 12 — not a lead-back edge. Sutton weeks 3-5 yards are 118, 81, 99 (the listed 6 is outside that sum); hot, but passed because Powers out and the lead-and-run script are the skill's own deep-WR kill. Franklin 17 targets, 98 yards, 192 air (inefficient; last4 89, 8, 55, 35) and Mims last4 24, 4, 69, 10 are boom-bust. Engram weeks 3-5: 13 targets, 62 yards, under a 25.5 line despite the coverage help. NYJ: Wilson last4 50, 84, 82, 71 vs 82.5, so 3 of 4 miss, and a throw-more script fights an under — pass. Hall rush last4 29, 21, 81, 113 vs 81.5, L3 average 71.7, but the trend is up and Denver is without Elliss with Roach questionable — under is script-plausible and not stamped. Allen last4 rush 9, 11, 30, 26 vs 18.5, backup, pass. Reynolds 6 targets, 29 yards L3, pass. Mason Taylor: weeks 3-5 are 25 targets and 150 yards, which is 18+65+67; the listed 5 is the older game. Two of those three crush 20.5, one (18) misses; 6.0 yards per target on 25 targets is volume, not a one-play spike.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. Taylor finished under 20.5 because the 18-yard game in the weeks 3-5 window was the role that showed up: Fields kept scrambling (108 rush yards over those three games), Wilson took the trailing targets (31 already), and Taylor never got past a handful of looks. Dobbins finished under 79.5 because Ben Powers was out, YPC fell off the 5.6 he posted on 47 carries, Harvey took the 20-carry share he already had, and a competitive game never produced the late clock-kill series a -7.5 favorite needs — he landed on the 79 that already missed this number. That counter is stronger on Dobbins than on Taylor, which is why Dobbins is a lean and Taylor is the leg that stays. Sutton over 81.5 is the Monday regret if it cashed, but stacking him with Dobbins would have been two legs that need opposite late scripts.
slip_story: One story: Denver leads and runs, the Jets trail and throw. Dobbins rushyds over is the favorite clock stack; Taylor recyds over is the dog-throws stack. They win together in the base script and still both have a path in the competitive flip. Do not add Sutton, Franklin or Mims overs (they need Denver to throw deep, which Powers out and a Dobbins clock-kill both cut). Do not add Hall rush over or a game over; Hall rush under would fit this story but was not stamped because 81 and 113 plus Elliss Out make the counter as strong as the read. No TDs, one market per player, two legs.
